flagship.headline: Top of the Pops launches on the BBC with Dusty Springfield
flagship.summary_line_1: Top of the Pops was first broadcast on BBC television on Wednesday, January 1, 1964, at 6:35 pm from Dickenson Road Studios in Manchester, hosted by Jimmy Savile, according to the Top of the Pops Archive.
flagship.summary_line_2: Dusty Springfield's I Only Want to Be with You was the first song performed, with the Rolling Stones, the Dave Clark Five and the Hollies also on the bill, and the clip below is that song from her Topic channel.

events.headline: Moon Mullican dies at 57
events.summary_line_1: Moon Mullican, the Texas country and western singer and pianist nicknamed the King of the Hillbilly Piano Players, died in Beaumont, Texas, on January 1, 1967, according to the Museum of the Gulf Coast and Birthplace of Western Swing.
events.summary_line_2: He had suffered a heart attack on New Year's Eve, and his tombstone carries the title of his 1950 hit I'll Sail My Ship Alone, which is the clip below from his Topic channel.

events.headline: Simon & Garfunkel reach No. 1 on the Hot 100 with The Sounds of Silence
events.summary_line_1: Simon & Garfunkel' The Sound of Silence jumped from No. 5 to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 dated January 1, 1966, after entering the chart at No. 80 on November 20.
events.summary_line_2: It held the top spot for two weeks, and the clip below is the single from the duo's official VEVO channel.

events.headline: The Beatles jump to No. 2 with We Can Work It Out
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles' We Can Work It Out leapt from No. 11 to No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 dated January 1, 1966, after entering the chart at No. 36 on December 18.
events.summary_line_2: Only Simon & Garfunkel stood above it that week, and the clip below is the song from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beatles climb to No. 18 with Day Tripper
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles' Day Tripper moved from No. 28 to No. 18 on the Billboard Hot 100 dated January 1, 1966, after entering the chart at No. 56 on December 18.
events.summary_line_2: It was the other side of the same single as We Can Work It Out, and the clip below is the song from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beach Boys reach their peak with The Little Girl I Once Knew
events.summary_line_1: The Beach Boys' The Little Girl I Once Knew rose to its No. 20 peak on the Billboard Hot 100 dated January 1, 1966, after entering the chart at No. 69 on November 27.
events.summary_line_2: It slid to No. 34 the following week, and the clip below is the song from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Animals reach their peak with It's My Life
events.summary_line_1: The Animals' It's My Life rose to its No. 23 peak on the Billboard Hot 100 dated January 1, 1966, after entering the chart at No. 87 on November 6.
events.summary_line_2: The clip below is the song from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beach Boys debut on the Hot 100 with Barbara Ann
events.summary_line_1: The Beach Boys' Barbara Ann entered the Billboard Hot 100 dated January 1, 1966 at No. 81.
events.summary_line_2: It had climbed to No. 58 by the chart dated January 8, and the clip below is the song from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: Bob Dylan debuts on the Hot 100 with Can You Please Crawl Out Your Window?
events.summary_line_1: Bob Dylan's Can You Please Crawl Out Your Window? entered the Billboard Hot 100 dated January 1, 1966 at No. 99.
events.summary_line_2: It had risen to No. 87 by the chart dated January 8, and the clip below is the mono single version from his VEVO channel.

events.headline: The Beatles open 1965 with two shows at the Hammersmith Odeon
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played two shows at the Hammersmith Odeon in London on January 1, 1965, at 6:15 pm and 8:45 pm, the seventh night of Another Beatles Christmas Show, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: She's a Woman was the B-side of their current single I Feel Fine, and the clip below is that song from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: Top of the Pops launches on the BBC with Dusty Springfield
events.summary_line_1: Top of the Pops was first broadcast on BBC television on Wednesday, January 1, 1964, at 6:35 pm from Dickenson Road Studios in Manchester, hosted by Jimmy Savile, according to the Top of the Pops Archive.
events.summary_line_2: Dusty Springfield's I Only Want to Be with You was the first song performed, with the Rolling Stones, the Dave Clark Five and the Hollies also on the bill, and the clip below is that song from her Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beatles play the Astoria Theatre on New Year's Day
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Astoria Theatre in Finsbury Park, London, on January 1, 1964, the seventh night of The Beatles Christmas Show, with Billy J. Kramer and the Dakotas, Cilla Black, the Fourmost and Tommy Quickly on the bill, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: Their single I Want to Hold Your Hand was their latest release, and the clip below is that song from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beach Boys record the backing track for Fun, Fun, Fun
events.summary_line_1: The Beach Boys recorded Fun, Fun, Fun on New Year's Day 1964 at United Western Recorders in Hollywood, with drummer Hal Blaine and saxophonist Steve Douglas joining the band, according to uDiscover Music.
events.summary_line_2: Vocals and overdubs followed on January 8 or 9, and the single came out on February 3, 1964, and reached No. 5 on the Hot 100, as the clip below from the band's Topic channel shows.

events.headline: The Beatles audition for Decca Records and are turned down
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles auditioned at Decca Studios in West Hampstead, London, on January 1, 1962, playing fifteen songs in just under an hour, according to the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: Decca chose Brian Poole and the Tremeloes instead, per This Day in Music, and the clip below is Like Dreamers Do from the audition, from the band's Topic channel.
